notes: The installer stopped declaring victory ten seconds in. RunPod answers 404 for a pod during the first few seconds while it is still being provisioned, and the watcher took that as the pod having finished and deleted itself — so an eighteen-gigabyte download was announced as done almost immediately, and the check that followed found nothing. A pod is now only considered gone once it has answered as gone twice in a row and has had time to exist at all; the first unanswered poll says so in the log instead. The check that runs after the pod really does disappear now looks in the folder each file was bound for rather than only in the LoRA folder, so a Kontext install can actually be seen succeeding, and when something is genuinely missing it says to wait and tap Install again rather than pointing at the wrong screen. The progress line also names the download size instead of talking about LoRAs.
